parts: Sorry for the annoyance, just noticed, that Apple Mail made me somewhat unreadable. Here is the content of the mail again, the formula now in Latex code:

Dear list-members,

I would like to fit the following model to a ggplot:

Y = - k \ln(1 - X/N), where N = \sumX.

I was trying this with stat_function as below, but to no avail. The code represents the solution with the least error informations.

mod_1_fit <- stat_function(data = Frequencies,
aes(x = A, y = B),
#geom = "line",
#fun = -log(1-x/sum(A))*mod_1_res[4,3],
fun = log(1-A/sum(A))*mod_1_k,
colour = "red")

I am new to R, to statistics, and to model fitting, and made my way through trial and error. Unfortunately, I don't know how to interprete the error notice.

"Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'A' not found" 


If this helps, the plot is transformed via coord_trans("log,"log", c(.5, sum(A)), c(.5, sum(A)).

Testing the curve alone, it works well in base graphics, so my best guess is that I am misunderstanding some of the intricacies of stat_function().

Thanks for your help!

K.M.
 
I found that stat_function required a starting point at the origin, but I thought this would not be affected by the coord_trans() command.

Kaz.
